transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Um, I guess what finally made me come in is that my appetite has just been all over the place for months now. 

There are these stretches where I just skip dinner entirely, and I've been losing weight without even trying to. And then other nights, I just end up picking at crackers or having a bowl of cereal because... well, the thought of actually cooking a real meal for myself just feels completely pointless lately.
When you skip meals or eat very little, is it because you’re afraid of gaining weight or concerned about your body shape?

No, not at all. It really has nothing to do with my weight or... or how my body looks. I'm not trying to diet or anything like that. It’s honestly just that I don't have the interest, or I guess the energy, to eat. Food just doesn't really appeal to me right now.
Have you been feeling sad, down, or depressed most of the day lately?

No, I wouldn't really say I feel sad. Um... I haven't noticed feeling depressed or down most of the day. It's really just what I mentioned, that I just don't seem to have the energy or interest to do things like make dinner. But no, not sad.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in activities that you usually enjoy?

Yes, I think so. I mean, I still go through the motions of things I used to love doing, like watering the garden or showing up to my book club. But most of the time, it just feels... flat. I don't really get any enjoyment out of it anymore. I usually end up leaving early, or sometimes I just don't even bother starting at all.
Did these changes in your appetite and enjoyment begin after a significant stressful event or major change in your life?
Yes, I suppose it did. Um... this has all been going on since my divorce was finalized. That was about a year and seven months ago.
Do your loss of interest and reduced appetite happen mainly when you’re thinking about the divorce, or do they occur broadly regardless of the divorce?

Um... I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't noticed if it happens specifically when I'm actively thinking about the divorce. I haven't really paid attention to a pattern like that... it just sort of feels like how things are for me right now.
Are you still experiencing significant distress specifically because of the divorce today?

I don't think so, no. I mean, it was hard at the time, of course, but I've accepted it. I'm not really dwelling on it or upset about the divorce itself anymore. It's just... everything else still feels off.
Have you been having trouble concentrating lately?

Yes, I have. At work, during case reviews, I find myself having to reread the same notes several times just to process them. And making decisions has been surprisingly hard. Even simple things, like deciding which client's call to return first, or just figuring out what to buy for dinner... it can take me an embarrassing amount of time lately.
Have you been feeling tired or lacking energy most days?

Yes, I have. Most days, actually. Even on days when my caseload isn't unusually heavy, I just... I feel like I am dragging my body through the hospital. And by the time I get home, I'm just too tired to do much of anything. I don't cook, I skip my stretching, and I can't even bring myself to answer personal text messages. The energy just isn't there right now.
Have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead or of hurting yourself?

No, I don't have a plan to hurt myself or anything like that. But... I do sometimes catch myself thinking that it would just be a relief not to wake up. And honestly, that scares me a bit. If one of my clients said that to me, I know I would take it very seriously. So... yeah, those thoughts are there.

Although onset followed divorce, the symptoms are broad, not specifically tied to ongoing distress about the divorce, and are better explained by a major depressive episode than adjustment disorder or an eating disorder.
